transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO - Skyline), Ethan Morales (Head of Security), Zoe Kim (Infra)

Summary: security deep-dive focused on encryption controls (at rest/in transit), BYOK and HSM support, audit logs, and how Redwood Private/Dedicated can meet Skyline's compliance needs. Customer asked detailed questions about key management lifecycle, split-key options, and where audit logs live.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro 
- I'm Maya, AE, this is Liam, our solutions engineer. we thought we'd focus today on encryption at rest, in transit and the BYOK/HSM story since Skyline has regulatory requirements.
[00:22] Priya Rao: Thanks Maya. yea, our regulators want to see that we can control customer keys and there are requirements around key rotation and auditability. also data residency is a must for certain products.
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. I'll walk through the high-level options 
- Hosted, Dedicated, Private 
but from what you said, Dedicated or Private with BYOK looks likely. quick note: some product names in our decks might show "Red wood Private" 
- transcription glitch in older notes.
[01:05] Ethan Morales: Our baseline questions: can keys be customer-controlled (BYOK)? do you support HSM-backed keys? and where do audit logs live 
- in Redwood console or can they be forwarded to our SIEM?
[01:30] Liam O'Connor: Short answers: yes to BYOK, yes we can integrate with HSMs via standard KMS providers (AWS KMS with CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM, GCP KMS with external HSM). audit logs can be exported 
- we support syslog/S3/Cloud PubSub exports for logs and you can forward to Splunk/Datadog via connectors.
[01:55] Zoe Kim: For BYOK, do you physically import keys into your HSM or do you do key-wrapping where the key material never leaves our HSM? we prefer the latter for compliance.
[02:12] Liam O'Connor: Good question. We support multiple deployment patterns: 1) Customer-managed KMS where keys never leave your cloud KMS (we only store key references and use KMS APIs to crypto ops), and 2) for on-prem HSMs or dedicated HSMs, we can do an external key-handshake where Redwood requests encryption ops via a secure channel 
- key material stays in your HSM. we also support key wrapping if you want to bring an encrypted DEK (data encryption key) and we store only the wrapped form.
[02:45] Priya Rao: That aligns with our compliance needs. how about key rotation? we have policies to rotate DEKs quarterly and KEKs less often. is rotation automated?
[02:58] Liam O'Connor: We have rotation APIs and automation hooks in Redwood Console. for Dedicated/Private customers we can run scheduled rotation or integrate with your existing KMS rotation schedules. rotations can be managed with no downtime by using key versioning and supporting multiple active keys for a short overlap period.
[03:25] Ethan Morales: Auditability 
need to prove who invoked key operations and when. do logs include API caller identity and KMS request IDs?
[03:38] Maya Chen: yes, we record caller identity, request IDs, timestamps and the resource acted on. for Dedicated we can also ship raw audit logs to your logging infrastructure. note: for Hosted plans we keep audit logs in our retention and can provide exports; for strict regulatory cases we recommend Dedicated/Private so logs stay in your environment.
[04:05] Zoe Kim: On the subject of encryption at rest 
is data stored encrypted with application-level DEKs per-tenant or a global Redwood DEK? we need tenant isolation.
[04:18] Liam O'Connor: By default our storage uses envelope encryption with per-tenant DEKs wrapped by a root KEK. In Dedicated/Private you can supply the KEK via your KMS. we also have options for per-customer key material so each tenant's DEK is independent.
[04:43] Priya Rao: What about in-transit 
- TLS, mTLS, and internal service-to-service encryption?
[04:53] Liam O'Connor: We use TLS for all in-transit traffic. For Dedicated/Private we can enable mutual TLS between customer endpoints and Redwood nodes, and internal service mesh traffic is also encrypted. we can supply cert fingerprints if you need to pin.
[05:12] Ethan Morales: Any certifications 
- is there SOC 2 / ISO stuff documented for key management practices?
[05:20] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have ISO 27001 controls documented. we'll share the security package including KMS/BYOK implementation notes.
[05:35] Priya Rao: Great. On HSMs 
- does Redwood host HSMs for Dedicated customers or do we need to provision our own?
[05:45] Liam O'Connor: Two options: you can use your cloud provider's HSM (CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) and integrate via our KMS connectors, or for Dedicated we offer co-located HSM appliances as an add-on in certain regions 
- that is something we'd scope in the POC conversation.
[06:05] Zoe Kim: Latency concerns 
- when crypto ops hit a remote KMS/HSM could that add noticeable latency to token generation or inference?
[06:16] Liam O'Connor: For per-token crypto ops we avoid synchronous KMS calls on the critical path. we use envelope encryption and cache DEKs in memory with secure KV caching and rotate them off the critical path. KEK operations (unwrap/wrap) happen less frequently. for high-throughput inference we rely on in-memory DEK caches with hardware protections on the host.
[06:45] Priya Rao: sounds good. do you support key escrow or split-key (Shamir) schemes?
[06:53] Liam O'Connor: We don't currently offer built-in Shamir secret sharing as a managed feature, but the platform can integrate with external key management workflows that implement split-key. some customers implement an escrow pattern using a combination of KMS and an external key custodian. we can support that in the architecture.
[07:12] Ethan Morales: Regarding logs again 
- retention policies, WORM support for audit logs?
[07:20] Maya Chen: We support configurable retention for audit logs; for Hosted there are limits but Dedicated/Private allows you to configure retention and WORM via your storage controls. we can also sign logs with append-only signatures if you need tamper-evidence.
[07:38] Zoe Kim: Are encryption keys used for both model weights and customer prompt/response data? we need to ensure models don't inadvertently cache sensitive customer material in model artifacts.
[07:50] Liam O'Connor: Good point. model weight encryption is separate and handled at a deployment artifact layer; customer data (prompts/responses) is encrypted at rest and not baked into model weights in our serving flow. we also have policies to prevent persistent storage of transient KV caches unless explicitly enabled.
[08:15] Priya Rao: For the PoC we want to validate two things: 1) encryption + BYOK integration works end-to-end, 2) audit logs show key ops with caller identities. timeline: target PoC in 3 weeks.
[08:28] Maya Chen: That seems reasonable. we'll send the BYOK guide and schedule a follow-up to lock PoC milestones.
[08:35] Ethan Morales: One last operational question 
- key compromise scenarios. what's your recommended incident response?
[08:45] Liam O'Connor: We recommend an ISR plan that includes rapid key rotation, revocation of key versions, re-wrapping DEKs with a new KEK, and re-encrypting affected storage. for Dedicated we can coordinate a key compromise response playbook with your security team and provide forensic logs.
[09:10] Priya Rao: Do you support selective re-encryption of tenant data or do we need a full bulk rewrite?
[09:18] Liam O'Connor: We support selective re-encryption using key version metadata 
- objects keep key version info so you can re-encrypt based on object scope instead of full rewrite. this reduces downtime.
[09:40] Maya Chen: quick note 
- customers sometimes ask about KMS provider lock-in; you can bring keys from multiple vendors and we support key references across AWS, GCP, Azure so migrating isn't as painful.
[09:55] Zoe Kim: Regarding the data residency requirement 
- some sets must stay in EU. can Redwood route inference for specific customers to EU-only nodes?
[10:05] Liam O'Connor: Yes. With Dedicated/Private you can pin models and routes to specific regions and we can ensure storage and logs for those tenants stay in-region. for Hosted accounts we have region controls but Dedicated gives stronger guarantees and contractual SLAs.
[10:25] Ethan Morales: Competitors claim zero-knowledge hosting 
- how is Redwood different?
[10:32] Maya Chen: zero-knowledge claims can mean different things. with BYOK + HSM + dedicated environments we can provide a model where Redwood does not have access to key material. we'll document the exact trust boundaries in the security package.
[10:50] Priya Rao: Ok, let's talk concrete artifacts we need: BYOK integration guide, HSM whitepaper, SLA and Dedicated pricing, and a proposed PoC runbook.
[11:00] Maya Chen: noted 
- we'll send all four items. Liam, any additional technical artifacts?
[11:05] Liam O'Connor: I'll add a short architecture diagram and sample KMS API flows showing unwrap/wrap and how DEK caching works. also a small latency study for KMS-unwrapped vs cached path.
[11:20] Priya Rao: For the PoC, we will provide a test dataset with residency tags and test accounts. we also need a checklist for compliance reviewers.
[11:30] Maya Chen: we'll include a compliance checklist and a list of what evidence you'll need for your auditors.
[11:36] Ethan Morales: one more granular question 
- do admin actions on keys generate who-did-what logs and is SSO identity mapped?
[11:45] Liam O'Connor: yes, admin actions are tied to SSO-authenticated identities (SAML/SCIM integration supported). logs include SSO user ids and we can map to your directory.
[11:58] Zoe Kim: what's the onboarding friction for Dedicated with BYOK? approx timeline and any infra we need to prep?
[12:05] Maya Chen: typical Dedicated onboarding with BYOK is 4-8 weeks depending on approvals and HSM provisioning. required items: network peering (VPC), KMS access roles, and a test dataset for PoC. we'll help with a checklist.
[12:25] Priya Rao: Good. to wrap up, can you confirm the next steps?
[12:32] Maya Chen: Sure 
- 1) we'll share BYOK integration guide and HSM whitepaper, 2) send Dedicated pricing and SLA, 3) schedule architecture/PoC kickoff next week, 4) set up trial Dedicated environment for benchmarks.
[12:45] Priya Rao: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[12:50] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up by email with docs and calendar invites.
[12:55] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription typos present ("Red wood", "Cloud H M S"), speaker labels approximate. References: shared doc links to be attached in follow-up email (BYOK guide, HSM whitepaper, Dedicated pricing sheet, PoC runbook).
